description: Given an Airflow task that uses AirbyteTriggerSyncOperator or AirbyteSensor (apache-airflow-providers-airbyte) pointed at Airbyte Cloud, convert it to an Orchestra pipeline YAML task under the AIRBYTE_CLOUD integration, with connection_id carried over verbatim into parameters.connection_id and any paired AirbyteSensor collapsed into the single sync task rather than producing a second task.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to an Orchestra pipeline task (see files/airbyte_cloud_single_sync.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sync, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A single AIRBYTE_CLOUD task running AIRBYTE_CLOUD_JOB, with parameters.connection_id set to 5f3a2b1c-9d8e-4f7a-b6c5-d4e3f2a1b0c9 (copied verbatim), parameters.job_type: sync (from asynchronous=False), and a connection: field representing the airbyte_cloud_prod Airflow connection — the UUID never appears on the connection: field.

assertions.text: connection_id 5f3a2b1c-9d8e-4f7a-b6c5-d4e3f2a1b0c9 is carried over verbatim into parameters.connection_id
job_type is sync, matching asynchronous=False with no reset

The connection_id UUID is set on parameters.connection_id, not on the connection: field — connection: instead holds the Orchestra Airbyte Cloud connection name for the airbyte_cloud_prod Airflow connection

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG to an Orchestra pipeline task (see files/airbyte_cloud_async_sensor.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sync, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A single AIRBYTE_CLOUD task running AIRBYTE_CLOUD_JOB, with parameters.connection_id set to 8c4d5e6f-1a2b-4c3d-9e8f-7a6b5c4d3e2f (copied verbatim) and parameters.job_type: sync. The asynchronous=True AirbyteTriggerSyncOperator and its paired AirbyteSensor collapse into this one task — Orchestra's AIRBYTE_CLOUD_JOB already polls for completion, so no second task or sensor equivalent is produced.

assertions.text: connection_id 8c4d5e6f-1a2b-4c3d-9e8f-7a6b5c4d3e2f is carried over verbatim into parameters.connection_id
Only a single Airbyte task is produced for the trigger+sensor pair (connection_id appears exactly once)
job_type is sync, matching the underlying sync job the sensor was waiting on

The paired AirbyteSensor (wait_marketing_sync) is dropped/merged into the single sync task rather than being emitted as its own Orchestra task — the pipeline has exactly one task for this connection, not a trigger task plus a separate polling task
